title: Choose the visual world for Soni Khimraj Lalji Jewellers
question: The roll assigned The Mithai Box. Keep it, take my pick or the standard, or re-roll.

options.label: The Mithai Box
options.lineage: Mumbai sweet-shop gift boxes from Diwali, Dhanteras and weddings
options.thesis: The site is the shop's own festive gift box: lift the lid and the jewellery sits in compartments, with the name, address and phone printed where every box prints them.
options.viewport: A rani-pink lid fills the screen: the name foil-stamped in Devanagari and English, today's IBJA rate on the box's price sticker, and WhatsApp Mr. Soni as the main button.
options.risk: Can read as a sweet shop if the jewellery photos are weak; every compartment needs real gold in it.

raised.raise: Inks, not gradients: the box prints in two flat spot colours plus gold foil, and overlaps multiply; there are no gradients anywhere.
The Gold Dream Scheme's 12 months are one unbroken row of 12 compartments that scales and never wraps.
Empty compartments tell the truth: until a real photo exists, a slot shows a ghosted outline and 'Ask Mr. Soni for photos', never stock.
Each section leads with one object that is its label (a touchstone for old gold, a passbook for the scheme), and the text only confirms it.
The visit block prints Jivdaya Lane and its landmarks as the box's map, the way sweet shops print their branch addresses.
Only one foil element shines per screen: gold foil is reserved for the live thing (today's rate or the main action).

options.label: The Kankotri
options.lineage: Gujarati and Marathi wedding invitation cards (kankotri, lagna patrika)
options.thesis: The site reads like a family's wedding invitation: layered cards, a blessing line at the top, foil borders, and the visit to Jivdaya Lane as the venue block.
options.viewport: An invitation opens: the shop's blessing line, the name in Devanagari foil, 'You're invited to Jivdaya Lane' with the address and hours as the venue, and RSVP on WhatsApp.
options.risk: Familiar: Indian bridal sites (Rivaah) often land here, and it can feel wedding-only for daily wear and old-gold visitors.

options.label: Risograph web system
options.thesis: Fluorescent spot inks misregistered on toothy paper.
options.risk: Reads as an art-school zine to a family buying gold.
options.case: Loses on both axes: local families don't recognise Riso, and the misregistration blurs the rate and hallmark facts.
options.kept: Flat spot inks with no gradients.

options.label: Rhythm machine step row
options.thesis: Sixteen lit step keys under a chase light.
options.viewport: A step row as the page's one line.
options.risk: A music machine says nothing about a jeweller.
options.case: Loses on both axes overall, though the 12-month scheme maps neatly onto a step row.
options.kept: One unbroken 12-step row for the scheme.

options.label: Sticker album spread
options.thesis: Numbered slots where empty positions show what is missing.
options.viewport: A grid of numbered slots, some filled.
options.risk: Playful collecting feels off for bridal gold.
options.case: Loses on both axes as a whole world, but its honesty about missing photos fits a shop still waiting on its own pictures.
options.kept: Ghosted outlines where real photos aren't in yet.

options.label: Fletcher wit poster
options.thesis: One visual pun per section, cut paper and crayon.
options.viewport: One pun image owns the sheet.
options.risk: Wit can undercut trust when the purchase is gold.
options.case: Loses on both axes: puns obscure the rate and hallmark facts, and families don't read gold through jokes.
options.kept: Each section's object is its own label.

options.label: Sleeping city fold
options.thesis: Streets that crease into blankets under one night.
options.risk: Dreamy and slow for a quick rate check.
options.case: Loses on both axes, but the idea of a recognisable local map is worth keeping.
options.kept: A printed map of Jivdaya Lane and its landmarks.

options.label: Bioluminescent plankton wake
options.thesis: Living light that traces motion and fades.
options.viewport: A dark field lit by the pointer.
options.risk: WebGL and darkness; the opposite of a phone-first local shop.
options.case: Loses on both axes: 3D-like effects are out of scope and it's slow on mid-range phones.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern luxury jeweller site executed at full craft: white space, an editorial serif, full-bleed product photography and a sticky WhatsApp bar.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed bridal photo, the name in a fine serif, 'Visit our Ghatkopar shop' and WhatsApp as the buttons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other jewellers by design.
